description:
WHAT IT IS MADE OF. Every token is a small stack of large, flat, hard-edged geometric primitives drawn on a near-black ground and blended with partial transparency: squares, rotated squares (diamonds), regular hexagons, octagons and circles. There is no line work, no texture, no gradient, no noise, no type. The only tonal modelling in the entire collection comes from where translucent shapes overlap each other and build up value. Colour is a single narrow band of warm neutrals -- taupe, putty, oatmeal, bone -- against a flat charcoal-black field. Nothing is saturated; there is no hue decision anywhere, only value.

WHAT IT IS A PICTURE OF. Mostly nothing representational. It reads as a study in stacked planes -- like flat paper or acetate cut-outs laid over one another on a dark table, or an exploded diagram of a solid with its faces separated. The one exception is seed 9369, which by accident of geometry reads figuratively: a large grey disc with a smaller lighter disc inside it and a tiny highlight dot, which I read immediately as a moon, an eye, or a coin. The 512px single is that seed, and it is the only token in the set that a viewer would give a noun to.

THE TWELVE (9011, 9190, 9369, 9548, 9727, 9906, 10085, 10264, 10443, 10622, 10801, 10980). What they share: one large host primitive occupying the middle of the frame, one or two smaller primitives nested concentrically inside it, and a generous dark margin on all sides. What differs: which primitive is the host, and whether the token carries the one real gesture in the collection -- a diagonal staircase of small squares that steps away from the host shape like a comet tail or a sprocket run. Four of the twelve have it: 9548 (four steps to the upper-left), 9727 (steps to the upper-right), 10264 (a bright cluster crowding the upper-right corner), 10980 (steps to the upper-left). 9190 has a downward version of it. The remaining seven are quiet centred polygons. Ranked by incident: 10801 is the busiest (an octagon with several rotated squares tumbled inside it), 10264 and 9190 are the brightest (pale near-white clusters), and 10085 is close to empty -- a plain grey hexagon with a barely-visible hexagon at its centre and nothing else. 10443 (diamond with a circle in it) and 10622 (square with concentric squares) are nearly as bare.

ACROSS THE THREE MARKET STATES (seen on 9011, 9190, 9369, 9548). The change is principally SCALE plus BRIGHTNESS plus the length of the staircase. Stress contracts and darkens: 9369's disc shrinks to roughly a third of its neutral area and a faint diamond becomes visible behind it; 9548's four-step tail is amputated to a single stub; 9190 pulls in tight and its pale cascade drops to two blocks; 9011 loses its outer square almost entirely and the hexagon underneath becomes the dominant silhouette. Recovery does the opposite and overshoots neutral: everything grows toward the edges of the frame, the pale elements get paler, 9548's tail returns at full length and higher key, 9190's cascade becomes a bright slab running off the bottom of the tile, 9369's disc swells to nearly fill its cell. So: contraction and dimming under stress, expansion and brightening under recovery, with neutral sitting between them. It is monotone and legible, and it is the same transformation applied to every seed rather than a per-seed behaviour.

WHAT SURVIVES AT 120px. The silhouette of the host primitive, the presence or absence of the staircase, and the overall lightness. Everything else is gone. The nested interior shapes that give 9011, 10622, 10443 and 10085 what little internal event they have are invisible at browse size -- 10622 in particular collapses to a plain grey square. At 120 the twelve resolve into about four or five perceptual classes rather than twelve: plain grey polygon (9011, 9906, 10085, 10443, 10622, and largely 10801), polygon-with-tail (9548, 9727, 10980), bright cluster (10264, 9190), and disc (9369). The three-state row, by contrast, survives 120px very well: all four seeds are unmistakably three different images at thumbnail size, and the direction of change reads without needing the labels.

ARTEFACTS I CAN SEE. The staircase collides with the frame repeatedly and is cut by it: 9548's top block is sliced by the upper edge in both neutral and recovery, 10980's tail is cut off at the left edge, 10264's bright cluster is cut at the right edge, and 9190's cascade runs off the bottom in neutral and much worse in recovery. These read as the composition overflowing its viewBox rather than as a deliberate bleed, because the rest of each frame is empty dark margin -- the work is not otherwise using its edges at all. Elsewhere the drawing is clean: no mush, no stray hairlines, no vanishing strokes.

MY OVERALL IMPRESSION, unprompted. Disciplined and consistent, and very thin. It looks like the default output of a translucent-overlapping-polygons sketch: correct, calm, internally coherent, and largely without an idea beyond the transparency stacking itself. The market response is genuinely delivered and is the strongest thing here. The seed variation is the weakest -- take away the four staircase tokens and the remainder are the same gesture at different rotations.
